judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: Image link (tabindex=-1) in the 'Latest' rail wrapping figure > img alt='Collage of person holding toddler's hands on the left and smoky imagery on the right', beside a headline link to the same article. The CDP tree in the snapshot gives the link no name while the img inside has its alt as its name. I reproduced this in Edge 158 headless (Chromium): an img with alt inside a figure inside a link gives the link an empty name, while the same img without the figure, or inside a div, gives the alt. So the empty name is Chromium's real computation, not a collector artefact. Against it: under the accname algorithm (recursion into descendants, steps 2F/2H) and in spec-based checkers such as axe, the figure's img alt contributes, so the link would be named by the alt; screen readers in browse mode also read the inner graphic, so 'announces only link' overstates it. Whether spec-conformant markup that the dominant engine fails to name counts as a 4.1.2 failure is a point competent auditors would dispute, so I cannot say the element fails, and the label is uncertain. Even if the alt were taken as the name, it describes the photo rather than the destination, which is a 1.1.1/2.4.4 matter (R2), not this claim. The live HTML has the same markup (tabindex=-1, figure-wrapped img, no aria-label or title); images were lazy-loaded (state broken in the snapshot, loaded in the screenshot), which does not change the name, so captureDiffers is no.

The bar was off-screen when captured (it slides in on scroll), but it is focusable and in the accessibility tree, and the live markup is identical. The claim names this failure.
